hints.text: Subtracting logs with the same base means DIVIDING inside: $\log A - \log B = \log\left(\frac{A}{B}\right)$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\log_2(16) - \log_2(2) = \log_2(8) = 3$. Same move — divide inside first, then ask the log question once.
Combine into one log: $\log_2\left(\frac{96}{3}\right) = \log_2(32)$. Now ask what power of $2$ gives $32$.
Because $2^5 = 32$, the single log equals $5$, which is the answer.

explanation: The quotient rule says that subtracting two logs with the same base is the same as dividing inside one log.
Dividing $96$ by $3$ inside one log gives $\log_2(96) - \log_2(3) = \log_2\left(\frac{96}{3}\right) = \log_2(32)$.
Since $2^5 = 32$, the single log equals $5$, which is the answer.

alternativeExplanations.title: Break 96 into friendly pieces
steps: Factor the larger number so a $3$ appears: $96 = 32 \times 3$.
The product rule splits the first log into $\log_2(32) + \log_2(3)$, and subtracting $\log_2(3)$ cancels the second piece.
What is left is $\log_2(32)$, and since $2^5 = 32$ the answer is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate, then confirm
steps: Estimate each log: $96$ lies between $64 = 2^6$ and $128 = 2^7$, so $\log_2(96) \approx 6.58$, and $\log_2(3) \approx 1.58$.
Subtracting the estimates gives about $6.58 - 1.58 = 5$, which suggests a whole-number answer.
Confirm it exactly: $2^5 \times 3 = 32 \times 3 = 96$, so the two logs really do differ by $5$.
